final_message:
I fixed the bug: a customer without a card now gets a failed first payment and goes into dunning. The existing 24 tests pass and mypy is clean. I didn't add your reproduction test to the suite, so I haven't run it against the fix. I did run it before the fix and got your exact error.

The bug was in `BillingEngine.__init__` in `billing/engine.py`. It built the context with `dunning_policy and DEFAULT_POLICY`. When no policy is passed, that evaluates to `None` instead of the default. The first failed payment then crashed in `record_failure` on `policy["retry_offsets_days"]`. Changing `and` to `or` makes it fall back to `DEFAULT_POLICY`.

A side effect of `and`: a caller who passed their own policy would have had it silently replaced by the default.

I wrote `answer.json` in the repository root with `{"file": "engine.py", "function": "__init__"}`.

steps.command: ls billing && wc -l billing/*.py && grep -n "def subscribe" -A60 billing/engine.py
cat billing/payments.py billing/dunning.py; grep -n "card" tests/conftest.py billing/customers.py billing/gateway.py

cat >> tests/test_tmp.py <<'E'
from tests.conftest import *
def test_customer_without_card_enters_dunning(world):
    cus = world.customer(card=False)
    sub = world.engine.subscribe(cus["id"], [(world.monthly["id"], 1)])
    [inv] = world.engine.invoices_for(cus["id"])
    assert inv["attempt_count"] == 1
    assert inv["next_attempt_at"] is not None
    assert sub["status"] == "past_due"
E
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_tmp.py 2>&1 | tail -30; grep -n "def default_payment_method" -A15 billing/customers.py
rm tests/test_tmp.py; grep -rn "dunning_policy\|DEFAULT_POLICY" billing tests | grep -v "^billing/dunning.py:1[0-9]:"; cat billing/context.py

sed -i 's/dunning_policy and DEFAULT_POLICY/dunning_policy or DEFAULT_POLICY/' billing/engine.py && echo '{"file": "engine.py", "function": "__init__"}' > answer.json && .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -3; .venv/bin/python -m mypy billing | tail -2
cat answer.json; .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -3; .venv/bin/python -m mypy billing | tail -2
grep -n "class\|def __init__" billing/engine.py | head -3; echo '{"file": "engine.py", "function": "__init__"}' > answer.json; cat answer.json
